evidence.quote: match Json.field "version" document with ... Error $"Transfer files of version {v} cannot be read here."
Some held when not (held.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && held.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && held.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && held.Payments.IsEmpty)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The file format, the read checks and their order, and the refusal sentences are in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). The page rules are in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2): the 'only into new books' rule, the GitHub refusal, and the missing-files-pack refusal. The only Tier 3 change is mapping three kernel events to engine messages in AccountingWire. It makes no decision.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: Transfer.export and Transfer.read are pure and are documented 'Pure.' The export time comes from ctx.Now and the business date from businessToday, so the engine reads no clock. The download is requested as data (OfferDownload(name, "application/json", base64)) and is the only effect. Import goes through the existing `save` helper, which yields one SaveBooks effect. Nothing new touches I/O, clock or randomness below Tier 4.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Each fact has one definition: Schema, Version and stampFormat in Transfer.fs, the notTransfer sentence, and booksOnGitHubMessage, which is shared by both GitHub guards. The 'yyyy-MM-dd' format string appears at two sites in the engine, for the file name and the notice. It covers two different outputs and the copies agree, so I treat it as negligible. Export reuses Exports.dataVersion, Exports.Classification and LocalSnapshot.encode instead of redefining them.

evidence.quote: let contentsOf (r: Receivables) : Contents = { Customers = r.Books.Customers.Count; Invoices = r.Books.Invoices.Count; Payments = r.Payments.Count }
if fileVersion = decimal Version && declared <> Some counted then Error "The books in this file do not match its contents."
match Transfer.read pasted with | Error why -> ...

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The counting rule, the version 1 and 2 acceptance rule, and the contents-mismatch refusal are all in Transfer.fs (Tier 2). The preview is built in the Tier 2 engine's view projection from Transfer.read and the books' own counts (t.Contents). The preview only formats pluralisation and text. Tier 3 and the page do no re-deriving.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect. contentsOf and the extended read and export are pure. The preview is a pure projection of model.BooksTransfer, so it is testable without any host. No clock, I/O or randomness is introduced.

evidence.quote: | Error why -> $"This file cannot be imported: {why}"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have a single authority, contentsOf. It is used both when exporting and when checking a file, and the preview reads it from Transferred.Contents. The version definition is also single: Version = 2 plus oldestVersion. However, the refusal sentence 'This file cannot be imported: <why>' is now written twice in the engine, once in the BooksTransferImported handler from change set 1 and once in booksTransferPreview. The 'yyyy-MM-dd' export-date rendering is also restated, in the import notice and in the preview. The copies agree today but could drift, since neither is a shared helper.
